speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand what is happening, have you noticed any vision changes or difficulty speaking in addition to these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the Spinal Cord (likely due to Vitamin B12 deficiency). The combination of acute subacute leg weakness, ataxia (unsteady gait), and cognitive/behavioral changes (forgetfulness, paranoia) in a 44-year-old male is highly suggestive of neurological demyelination affecting the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts. REQUEST TEST: Serum Vitamin B12 level, methylmalonic acid, and homocysteine.
